on_shelf.label: History of Philosophy, General Standpoint of the Scholastics
on_shelf.text: But the divine kingdom, the dwelling-place of the dead, was to be reached only through the gate of death; yet the natural world was dead to an equal degree—all that lived in it was the vision of that other world, and hope—it had no present. It was of no avail to introduce mediators as a connecting link, the Virgin Mary, or the dead in a world beyond.

on_shelf.label: History of Philosophy, Socrates
on_shelf.text: This is not a moderation which exists in the least possible enjoyment, no aimless abstemiousness and self-mortification, but a power belonging to consciousness, which keeps its self-possession in bodily excess. We see from this that we have not to think of Socrates throughout after the fashion of the litany of moral virtues.

typed_records.words: Good morning, Ramesh. The tea is welcome. I trust the household is quiet this morning; I shall take my reading to the step before the sun grows too strong.

typed_records.speaker: Ramesh
typed_records.words: Morning, Shri Hegel. Yes, quiet as a library. I’ll have the breakfast ready by seven, if you don’t mind.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: I shall begin the walk now, Ramesh. Thank you for the tea. I will return before the heat settles.

typed_records.speaker: Ramesh
typed_records.words: All right, sir. The gate is unlocked, so you just walk out. I'll keep the sambar warm.
